1.note:
# General Information:

In this chapter, Yahweh speaks about Jerusalem as if the city were his unfaithful bride. He describes her growth from infancy to adulthood. The city represents the people who live there. (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

2.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

3.note: These two phrases share similar meanings. Yahweh speaks of when people founded the city as if it were the city’s birth. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

3.q: your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite
3.note: The Amorites and Hittites were both pagan people groups who lived in the land before the people of Israel conquered it. Yahweh speaks of Jerusalem’s father and mother belonging to these people groups to express that she was born into idolatry.

4.q: your mother did not cut your navel
4.note: Here “navel” refers to the umbilical cord that is attached to the navel. Alternate translation: [you mother did not cut your umbilical cord]

5.q: No eye had compassion for you
5.note: Here the word “eye” represents the person who sees. Alternate translation: [Nobody who saw you had compassion for you]
Alternate translation: [because your parents hated you]

5.q: you were thrown out into the open field
5.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [your parents threw you out into the open field]

6.note: Yahweh is walking near the newborn baby.

6.q: I said to you in your blood
6.note: The implicit information can be supplied from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: [I said to you as you were lying in your blood]

7.q: I made you grow like a plant in a field
7.note: Here Yahweh compares growing quickly with the way a plant grows quickly.
These two phrases share similar meanings. They both refer to her growing and becoming taller. Alternate translation: [You matured and grew taller]

7.q: you became the jewel of jewels
7.note: Here the woman, who represents Jerusalem, is spoken of as if she had become the finest of all jewels, that is, as if she had become the most beautiful of all women.

7.q: you became the jewel of jewels
7.note: Some modern versions translate “You became old enough to wear jewels.”
These two words mean the same thing. Alternate translation: [completely naked]

8.note: The word “see” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

8.q: the time of love came for you
8.note: This is to say that Yahweh sees the young woman is old enough to be married.

10.note: “beautiful clothes.” To embroider is to sew a design into a piece of cloth.

11.note: Alternate translation: [I put jewelry on you]

13.q: you were adorned with gold and silver, and you were dressed in fine linen
13.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I adorned you with gold and silver, and dressed you in fine linen]

14.q: Your fame went out among the nations
14.note: Alternate translation: [Many people in many nations knew who you were]

15.q: you trusted in your own beauty
15.note: Alternate translation: [you placed your confidence in your own beauty]
Yahweh speaks of Jerusalem as if the city were an unfaithful wife who sleeps with other men in exchange for payment.

15.q: you poured out your acts of prostitution
15.note: Yahweh speaks of Jerusalem’s immoral actions as if they were liquids and of committing those actions repeatedly as if it were pouring those liquids from a container. Alternate translation: [you repeatedly committed your acts of prostitution]

15.q: so that your beauty became his
15.note: This Hebrew phrase is translated in many different ways by various modern versions. For example, some Bibles read “so that you gave yourself to him” or “his it was”

17.note: Alternate translation: [statues of men] or [idols that look like men]

17.q: you did with them as a prostitute would do
17.note: This could mean: (1) this is a polite way to say the young woman was sleeping with the male figures. Alternate translation: [you slept with them] or (2) this is a metaphor in which Yahweh speaks of her worshiping the figures as if she were sleeping with them. Alternate translation: [you worshiped them] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

19.note: Alternate translation: [placed as an offering in front of them]

20.q: you sacrificed them to the images to be devoured as food
20.note: Here Yahweh speaks of something that the people of Israel had actually done. They sacrificed their children to pagan idols. In these ancient pagan sacrifices, the people believed that the gods would eat the food that they offered to them. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you sacrificed them to the images so that those images could devour them as food] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

20.q: Are your acts of prostitution a small matter?
20.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize that the woman is acting as if her prostitution was not bad enough and so she decided to sacrifice her children as well. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [You must think that your acts of prostitution are a small matter.] or [I do not think your acts of prostitution are a small matter.]

21.q: made them pass through the fire
21.note: Here Yahweh speaks of something that the people of Israel had actually done. They sacrificed their children to pagan idols. It is implicit that she put them into the fire in order to offer them as burnt offerings to her images. Alternate translation: [sacrificed them as burnt offerings]

22.note: These two words mean the same thing. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 16:7. Alternate translation: [completely naked]

24.q: you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public place
24.note: This could mean: (1) she could worship her idols or (2) she could practice her prostitution.

25.q: at the head of every road
25.note: Yahweh speaks of the beginning of a road as if it were its head. Alternate translation: [at the beginning of every road]

27.note: The word “see” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

27.q: I will strike you with my hand
27.note: Here “hand” represents power. Alternate translation: [I will use my power to strike you]
Yahweh speaks of stopping the supply of food as if it were cutting off the food. Alternate translation: [stop your food supply]

27.q: I will hand your life over
27.note: Here “life” represents the person. Alternate translation: [I will hand you over]

Here Yahweh speaks of the cities of Philistia as if they were the daughters of the Philistines. The cities represent the people who live there. Alternate translation: [the Philistine people] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

30.q: How sick is your heart … that you would do all these things, deeds of a shameless prostitute?
30.note: Yahweh asks the rhetorical question in order to rebuke Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [Your heart must be very sick … that you would do all these things, deeds of a shameless prostitute!]

Here the word “heart” represents the will and emotions. Yahweh speaks of her inability to control her desires as if her heart were sick. Alternate translation: [How weak-willed are you] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

31.q: built your mounds … made your lofty shrines
31.note: This could mean: (1) she could worship her idols or (2) she could practice her prostitution. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 16:24.

31.q: at the head of every street
31.note: Yahweh speaks of the beginning of a street as if it were its head. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 16:25. Alternate translation: [at the beginning of every street]

32.q: you accept strangers instead of your husband
32.note: This refers to accepting someone to sleep with her. Alternate translation: [you accept strangers into your bed instead of your husband] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

36.q: you have poured out your lust
36.note: Yahweh speaks of Jerusalem’s lust as if it were liquid and of committing actions repeatedly to gratify that lust as if it were pouring that liquid from a container. Alternate translation: [you repeatedly committed actions to gratify your lust]
Some modern versions translate “poured your wealth out.”

36.q: you gave them your children’s blood
36.note: This refers to killing children as a sacrifice to idols.

37.note: The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

37.q: so they see all your nakedness
37.note: Stripping a person naked in front of others was an action intended to humiliate the person. The word “nakedness” can be translated as an adjective. Alternate translation: [so they can see you completely naked] (See also: [Abstract Nouns](ta:figs-abstractnouns))

38.note: This phrase represents murder in any form. Alternate translation: [murder]

38.q: I will bring on you the bloodshed of my anger and passion
38.note: Here “bloodshed” represents murder in any form. This could mean: (1) Yahweh speaks of punishing her for murder as if he were bringing bloodshed upon her. Alternate translation: [In my anger and passion, I will punish you for committing murder] or (2) Yahweh speaks of putting her to death as if he were bringing bloodshed upon her. Alternate translation: [In my anger and passion, I will shed your blood] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

39.q: I will give you into their hands
39.note: Here “hands” represents power or control. Alternate translation: [I will place you in their control] or [I will allow them to have power over you]

Possible meanings are that they will destroy (1) the place where she worshiped her idols or (2) the place where she practiced her prostitution. See how you translated “vaulted chamber” in Ezekiel 16:24.
These two words mean the same thing. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 16:7. Alternate translation: [completely naked]

41.q: will perform many acts of punishment on you
41.note: The word “punishment” can be translated with a verbal phrase. Alternate translation: [will punish you in many different ways]

41.q: in the sight of many women
41.note: Alternate translation: [where many women can see] or [while many women watch]

42.q: I will calm my fury against you; my anger will leave you
42.note: The words “fury” and “anger” refer to the punishment that Yahweh inflicts because he is angry. The two phrases mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [I will stop punishing you because I will no longer be angry with you] (See also: [Parallelism](ta:figs-parallelism))

43.note: This idiom means to remember. Alternate translation: [remember]

43.q: have made me shake with anger because of all these things
43.note: Here “shake” refers to a physical response that a person has when he is extremely angry. As Jerusalem was doing these things, she did not think about what Yahweh had done when she was young.
The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

44.note: The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

45.q: Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite
45.note: The Amorites and Hittites were both pagan people groups who lived in the land before the people of Israel conquered it. Yahweh speaks of Jerusalem’s father and mother belonging to these people groups to express that she was born into idolatry. See how you translated these phrases in Ezekiel 16:3.

46.q: Your older sister was Samaria … your younger sister was the one living south of you, that is, Sodom
46.note: Samaria and Sodom were both cities that Yahweh had judged for their idolatry and wickedness. Yahweh speaks of these cities being Jerusalem’s sisters to express that she belonged to a family that practiced idolatry and wickedness. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

47.q: You not only walked in their ways
47.note: The way a person lives is spoken of as if the person were walking on a path. Alternate translation: [You not only acted like them]
Here the words “behavior” and “practices” mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [copied the things that they did]

49.q: arrogant in her leisure, careless and unconcerned about anything
49.note: Yahweh describes Sodom as a rich woman who has more than enough food and lives in security.

49.q: She did not strengthen the hands of the poor and needy people
49.note: Here the word “hands” represents the people who work with their hands. The words “poor” and “needy” emphasize that these are people who cannot help themselves. Alternate translation: [She did not help the people who could not help themselves] (See also: [Doublet](ta:figs-doublet))

51.q: you have shown that your sisters were better than you
51.note: Yahweh uses this phrase three times to emphasize that the wicked cities of Samaria and Sodom were more righteous than Jerusalem.

52.q: Especially you, show your own shame
52.note: Yahweh uses this phrase twice to emphasize how shamefully the people of Jerusalem have acted.
Alternate translation: [be ashamed] or [bear your disgrace]

54.note: Alternate translation: [you will be ashamed] or [you will bear your disgrace]
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will humiliate you]

54.q: you will be a comfort to them
54.note: The noun “comfort” can be translated with a verbal phrase. Alternate translation: [you will comfort Sodom and Samaria]

55.q: your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored to their former condition
55.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will restore your sister Sodom and her daughters to their former condition]

55.q: Samaria and her daughters will be restored to their former estate
55.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will restore your sister Samaria and her daughters to their former estate]

55.q: you and your daughters will be restored to your former condition
55.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will restore you and your daughters to your former condition]

56.q: Sodom your sister was not even mentioned by your mouth
56.note: Here the word “mouth” represents the person who speaks. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [You did not even mention your sister Sodom] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

57.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [before you revealed your wickedness] or [before I revealed your wickedness]

57.q: you are an object of scorn
57.note: This refers to Jerusalem as something people talk badly about.

57.q: the daughters of Edom and to all the daughters of the Philistines
57.note: Here Yahweh speaks of the cities of Edom and Philistia as if they were the daughters of Edom and of the Philistines. The cities represent the people who live there. Alternate translation: [the Edomite people and to all the Philistine people] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

58.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, Yahweh, have declared]

59.q: despised your oath by breaking the covenant
59.note: Jerusalem broke her marriage covenant with Yahweh, thereby showing that she did not care about the oaths that she had made to him. Alternate translation: [despised your oath to me by breaking the covenant that you made with me]

60.note: This idiom means to remember. Alternate translation: [remember]

60.q: made in the days of your youth
60.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that I made with you when you were young]

62.note: When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

63.note: This idiom means to remember. Alternate translation: [remember everything]

63.q: you will no longer open your mouth to speak because of your shame
63.note: This means that Jerusalem will be too ashamed to speak.
